message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Submit dependencies to GitHub Dependency Graph
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - trunk
      - release/*
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Cache Gradle dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.gradle/caches
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') }}
      - name: Setup Gradle to generate and submit dependency graphs
        uses: gradle/actions/dependency-submission@8da46b539cd8fe6ab27ca75128919a18d757604c # v6.4.1",
  "rationale": "The workflow resolves Gradle dependencies through gradle/actions/dependency-submission on repeated pushes to trunk and release branches, but has no dependency cache. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern and the measured experiment batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200 (Gradle dependency cache; median elapsed 98s -> 78s, about 20.4% savings, all successes preserved) support adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.gradle/caches keyed on Gradle files. This caches dependency download state rather than build outputs, keeps the dependency-submission job and required checks intact, preserves permissions, and adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or new external network access beyond the standard GitHub Actions cache.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}


The workflow uses Gradle (gradle/actions/dependency-submission). So caching Gradle dependencies could apply. The pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE preconditions: "Repeated dependency fetching is measurable", "Cache inputs include lockfile and environment". The workflow runs on push to trunk and release/*, so repeated dependency fetching happens.
